episode_title: How to Communicate Under Pressure | CBS Sacramento’s Tony Lopez

real_qa.q: What techniques does Tony Lopez use to communicate effectively under pressure in live TV situations?
real_qa.r: Tony Lopez uses two key phrases to ensure intentional and thoughtful communication: 'now let's go through this carefully' to force yourself to slow down, and 'here's what I'd like you to know' to personalize the message. He emphasizes that energy equals intention, not speed or volume. He also practices breath work and staying present in the moment, using breathing techniques to manage anxiety during breaking news situations. His approach involves taking emotion out of the situation as much as possible while still delivering the message factually through the who, what, when, why, where, and how.
real_qa.requete: Tony Lopez communication under pressure techniques

real_qa.q: How did Tony Lopez handle reporting on Stanley Tukey Williams' execution at San Quentin Prison as a media witness?
real_qa.r: Tony Lopez was selected as the only Northern California TV anchor media witness to the execution of Stanley Tukey Williams, the notorious Crips gang leader, which took place in 2005 shortly after he arrived in California. He had to watch Williams walk into the death chamber at midnight and be put to death via lethal injection thirty minutes later, then immediately report on it for morning shows around California. He didn't discuss the experience with anyone, not even his wife, for six months because it was so difficult to witness. He had to remove emotion and rely on factual reporting of the sequence of events, the room, and details like the trouble the person administering the lethal injection had finding a vein.

guest.bio_context: Tony Lopez started at CBS Sacramento in 2005, coming from Denver where he launched the 4 p.m. newscast. He is originally from Los Angeles and moved to Sacramento because his wife's family is from the region. He has over 35 years in the broadcasting business and currently anchors the 5, 6, and 10 p.m. newscasts on CBS Sacramento (KOVR 13), while also developing a keynote speaking career focused on communication under pressure and embracing change.
